rules: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the MPV bit in mstatus is written with the value of the virtualization mode V at the time of the trap, and the MPP field is set to the nominal privilege mode at the time of the trap.
When an MRET instruction is executed, the virtualization mode V is set to the MPV bit in mstatus, unless the MPP field is 3, in which case V remains 0.
When a trap is taken into M-mode and a guest virtual address is written to mtval, the GVA field in mstatus is set to 1.
When a trap is taken into M-mode and the guest virtual address is not written to mtval, the GVA field in mstatus is set to 0.
When TVM is set to 1, HS-mode cannot access hgatp or execute HFENCE.GVMA or HINVAL.GVMA.
When TVM is set to 1, VS-mode accesses to vsatp or instructions HFENCE.VVMA or HINVAL.VVMA are unaffected.
The mstatus register is a superset of the HS-level sstatus register.
The mstatus register is not a superset of vsstatus.
When MPRV is 0, translation and protection behave as normal, and the current privilege mode applies.
When MPRV is 1, and MPV is 1, MPP is 0, the access is VU-level with two-stage translation and protection, and the HS-level MXR bit makes any executable page readable.

When MPRV is 1, and MPV is 1, MPP is 1, the access is VS-level with two-stage translation and protection, and the HS-level MXR bit makes any executable page readable, and vsstatus.SUM applies instead of the HS-level SUM bit.
When MPRV is 1, and MPV is -1, MPP is 3, the access is M-level with no translation.
Virtual-machine load/store instructions (HLV, HLVX, HSV) always act as though V=1 and the nominal privilege mode were hstatus.SPVP, overriding MPRV.
